This application coming on for orders this day, th e co  following:
 ORDER 01. Heard on I.A. No.7479 of 2024 which is an application for taking documents on record.
02. Documents may be relevant for proper adjudication of this application.
Therefore, I.A. No.7479 of 2024 is allowed and documents are taken on record.

03. This is the third (repeat) application filed by the applicant for grant of regular bail under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 relating to FIR No 238/2023 registered at P.S- Bhojpur District-Rajgarh (M.P.) for the offence under sections 363, 366, 376(2)(n) and 506 of IPC and sections 5(L) / 6 of POCSO Act.

The applicant is in custody since 08.07.2023.
04.

As per prosecution story, on 30.06.2023 brother of the minor Prosecutrix lodged an FIR at P.S.

sentences.text: During investigation it has been gathered that present applicant abducted the minor prosecutrix, took her with him to bus stand, railway station and Dhaba and committed repeatedly rape upon her.
Accordingly, the aforementioned offence has been registered against the applicant.
05. Learned counsel for the applicant contended that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this offence.
The applicant is in custody since 08.07.2023.
His earlier two bail applications have been dismissed as withdrawn.
The applicant is a permanent resident of District Rajgarh.
Final conclusion of trial shall take sufficient long time.

Under the above circumstances,
prayer for grant of bail may be considered on such terms and conditions, as this Court deems fit and proper.
06. Per-contra, learned Government Advocate for respondent / State opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection.
07. Counsel for objector also opposes the prayer and prays for its rejection.

08. Perused the impugned order of the trial Court as well as the case dairy.
09.

Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, arguments advanced by both the parties,
nature of allegation as also taking note of the fact that prosecutrix (PW-1) has been examined before the trial Court and she categorically stated in her statement that she is aged about 17 years 4 months and on the pretext of marriage the present applicant took her with him to Kota and applicant committed repeatedly rape upon her.
Her brother (PW/2), mother (PW/3) and brother (PW/5) also supported the case of the prosecutrix.
10. In view of the evidence available on record, this court is not inclined to grant bail to this applicant.
11. Hence, this third bail application filed by applicant under section 439 Cr.P.C. is hereby dismissed.
Certified copy, as per Rules.
